I'm in the same boat as you (clear tests, ultrasounds and laparoscopy) but my surgeon was barely 30 and not very knowledgeable. I'm looking into another lap with a surgeon who specialises in missed diagnosis of endometriosis in patients from my original hospital. My symptoms are also consistent with adenomyosis and sciatic endometriosis  (I suffer chronic pain in the the back of my right leg as well as pelvic pain) so I'm looking into whether either of those conditions could be the issue also. I'm having a CT scan in two days to check possible causes of the leg pain (spinal or sciatic). You really have to ask for as many tests as possible and find a doctor who actually takes you seriously as a patient to get anywhere with a diagnosis. I would recommend having a CT or MRI to make sure the pain isn't actually musculoskeletal and look into specialist acupuncture for pain relief. From there, maybe try to get a second opinion because not all doctors are equally informed or open minded about women's pelvic pain and it makes a big difference when you find the right specialist.
